_comment: Settings for cad_pick_place.py (CAD-part pick & place). World frame (meters): table top (Table_base.step) at z=0, robot base on its mounting plate at x=y=0, z=0.015; the table spans x -0.175..0.625, y -0.425..0.375.
_pick_xy_comment: Pick location (part's centre of mass) = big table hole (15, 0), the last open corner hole on the camera side (corner A; (16, 0) is under the pendant holder's bracket). Was [0.45, -0.10].

pick_station._comment: The part is picked from the pick station (pickstation.step, repo root). Its screw holes are put on the table's 40 mm hole grid, at the grid position nearest near_xy; the part sits on the column top, centre of mass over the column axis (this replaces pick_xy). enabled=false puts the part back on the table at pick_xy.
pick_station._seat_all_comment: true: EVERY part loaded in the web goes on the fixture the way main_part does (its STEP frame = the fixture's STEP frame), because all parts share the same mounting; only the pick points change. Each part's STEP must be exported in the fixture's coordinate frame. false: only seated_part goes on it.
pick_station._fixture_comment: Fixture.step bolted over the big corner hole at pick_xy (its 4 screw holes on the table grid). seated_part = the part made for it: it goes on the fixture as the two STEPs fit together (same CAD frame), held until the gripper closes. Other parts sit on the fixture top.

_debug_pause_comment: TEMPORARY TEST: Real Sim stops at the pick location (grasp pose) for this many seconds with the fingers at the approach opening (as in the Sim), then grips and carries on. 0 = off.
_place_release_comment: Safety at the drop location: the gripper lowers the part only to this height above the tray floor and opens there (the part drops the rest). 0 = set it down.

real_gripper._comment: Robotiq 2F-85 on the laptop's USB/RS-485 adapter, used by Real Sim when 'Real gripper' is ticked. speed / force 0..255 (64 = slow).

robot_base_offset_mm._comment: Calibration: where the REAL robot base is relative to the table, compared with the table CAD, as [x, y, z] mm (z > 0: it stands higher). The sim moves the arm by this, so the planner sends the real arm to the real part. Measure with: python calibrate_robot.py (touch a table hole with the closed fingertips). Was a guessed 20 mm height.

gripper_coupling_mm._comment: Coupling plate between the tool flange and the gripper on the real robot (mm), measured: 22 mm. Sim TCP from the flange = 22 + 10.8 (2F-85 base) + 145 = 177.8 mm (pendant tool point: 178.8).

collision_hulls._comment: How finely each part's collision shape follows the CAD (convex pieces, CoACD). 24 / 0.04 filled about a quarter of main_part's cup, so a finger planned inside it 'hit the part'; 48 / 0.02 leaves it open. The first run of a part converts it (about 30 s), then it is cached.

grasp_test._comment: Sim-to-real grasp check. enabled=true: Sim and Real Sim only go to the taught pick point, wait wait_before_close_s, close the gripper on the part in the fixture, hold hold_closed_s, open, back out along the approach line and go home. No lift, camera or place. false = the full pick, camera and place again.

pick_motion._comment: How the arm goes to pick. It starts at home (gripper pointing down at home_tcp_m, up over the middle of the table), turns the gripper there to the grasp orientation, travels in a straight line to the pre-grasp without turning, then approaches, grips and lifts slowly. Speeds are peak values (m/s for the TCP, rad/s for the joints). orient_first=false restores the direct move from home.

home_joints_deg._comment: Home taught on the real robot (pendant joint angles, degrees). Replaces home_tcp_m for that robot.
home_joints_deg._ec66_comment: Read from the real EC66 on 2026-11-18 (getRobotPos) with the gripper open (84 mm). Was [179.117, -79.731, -80.062, -107.723, -88.43, 17.775].

inspection._comment: After lifting, the robot shows the part to a camera on the table (front and right side for now; back, left side, top and bottom can be added back to views). point = where the part's centre of mass is held; yaw turns around the vertical axis, tilt > 0 shows the top, and tilt < 0 shows the bottom. Views the arm cannot reach are skipped.
